methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A deliberate community-led initiative to evaluate AI deployment across the Roanoke Valley signals grassroots capability-building outside metro hubs, suggesting distributed deep learning if accompanied by implementation resources and not just assessment.

signals.title: News | Maker of AI recyclable, garbage sorting systems ramps up in Virginia, Michigan - CoStar
signals.signal_reading: AI-powered waste sorting systems represent turnkey platform adoption that delivers operational efficiency without requiring deep technical capability—classic shallow-but-distributed deployment that could reach manufacturing and municipal sites across all regions.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's data center reversal in NoVA reflects infrastructure concentration reaching saturation limits, potentially redistributing future AI infrastructure investment—but only if policy mechanisms actively direct it beyond metro cores rather than simply pausing metro growth.

signals.title: Norfolk police officer uses AI to build music career and TikTok following - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: A Norfolk police officer using consumer AI tools for creative work exemplifies shallow-but-accessible adoption reaching non-tech workers in mid-tier metros—distribution without depth, enabled by platforms rather than training infrastructure.

signals.title: Unnecessary medical tests are raising healthcare costs. A group of Virginia doctors and researchers has shown it’s possible to change the approach.
signals.signal_reading: A multi-year research initiative reducing unnecessary medical testing demonstrates deep analytical capability deployment in healthcare, but published in JAMA by established research institutions suggests concentrated expertise rather than distributed community health system transformation.
